question.question: Can the documented synchronous same-batch send/write overlap be reconciled with Ready.Messages carrying responses whose support depends on that batch being durable?
question.importance: Publishing append support before its dependent entries are durable can affect A1 qualified support and later commitment. The source presently gives conflicting caller ordering instructions; this question does not establish an illegal implementation emission or a crash-loss history.
contexts: Latest HardState and previous-batch entries already persisted
event_paths: Follower append handling -> send queues MsgAppResp -> synchronous Ready returns response with new entries -> caller persists/sends according to selected contract

supporting_behavior_ids.B_ACK_COMMIT: Consumes successful responses as matched support toward commitment.
supporting_behavior_ids.B_ENTRY: Caller owns persistence and message release; shared RawNode internals do not override Node interface duties.

counterevidence: Ready.Entries and Ready.Messages expressly require same-batch entries persisted before message delivery.
RawNode.readyWithoutAccept explicitly relies on that stricter contract when moving msgsAfterAppend into Ready.Messages.
raft.send routes durability-dependent append/vote responses to msgsAfterAppend; async mode attaches them to ordered storage work instead.

README additionally orders Entries before HardState; when a nonempty HardState is persisted after entries this may prevent overlap for that batch, but does not reconcile the general same-batch permission when HardState is empty.
unknowns: Which same-batch ordering statement is authoritative for a legal synchronous caller?
Does the overlap permission intend only leader append requests rather than every Ready.Messages element? The text says all Messages, and the implementation does not tag a synchronous split.
No crash/restart history or actual prematurely delivered acknowledgement is claimed.
An authoritative clarification distinguishes the permitted message classes or resolves the same-batch persistence order for synchronous Ready.
Alternatively, identify an execution satisfying both documented ordering statements that still violates a separately sourced requirement.
question.trigger_rationale: Synchronous Ready merges non-self msgsAfterAppend into Messages without awaiting persistence internally. Both package usage and README permit sending Messages during same-batch entry persistence, whereas the typed Ready interface and implementation comment prohibit it. This is a normative caller-contract conflict, not missing source for the main call edge.

rationale: Pause only the synchronous ordering question because its limiting premise is the unresolved conflict between acquired caller contracts, not an unexecuted implementation schedule.
resume_conditions: Authoritative clarification restricts the same-batch overlap permission to particular message classes or resolves its conflict with Ready.Messages.
A concrete history legal under both ordering statements exposes a separately sourced discrepancy.

feedback.answered: The ordering Candidate is paused with precise contract-resolution conditions; the strict contract barrier and permissive wording remain visible. A separate source discriminator narrows the configuration-cancellation surface: Node and RawNode typed interfaces both say not to call ApplyConfChange for rejected changes, while the package usage text says to call with NodeID zero. Node.ApplyConfChange converts AsV2 and serializes the same raft.applyConfChange implementation reached by RawNode. A legacy zero-ID change becomes a one-element Changes list, so it is neither empty LeaveJoint nor multi-change EnterJoint; in a valid non-joint configuration Changer.Simple copies state and Changer.apply skips the zero ID. The voter/learner membership remains unchanged. Skipping the call also leaves membership unchanged. Pending configuration proposal admission compares pendingConfIndex with raftLog.applied; ordinary Advance/MsgStorageApplyResp moves applied regardless of whether ApplyConfChange was invoked. Thus the read source does not support a claim that skipping a rejected ApplyConfChange necessarily strands pending configuration admission.
remaining: The normative rejection instructions still differ, even though non-joint legacy membership effects can agree.
The zero-ID call executes switchToConfig and may recompute commitment, probe peers or abort a transfer; skipping it avoids those side effects, so full execution equivalence is not established.
Joint or ConfChangeV2 cancellation is outside this source explanation; replacing arbitrary V2 changes with empty data would instead mean LeaveJoint and must not be presumed a generic no-op.
Normal ReadIndex quorum acknowledgements across configuration changes and externally served read endpoints remain uncovered.
feedback.rationale: This source answer avoids inventing a configuration-stall obligation from inconsistent prose. It preserves both authoritative-looking statements and narrows actual effect uncertainty. The completed storage context-fence result and local singleton eligibility violation remain unchanged. Any further execution should target a concrete unresolved effect, rather than repeat the already explained non-joint membership no-op or assume the weaker synchronous send permission.
